Goal: Fix and verify every external data URL in the exercise notebooks of this folder (a git repo of Google Colab notebooks
for a HEP textbook). You HAVE network access in this run. Every URL you leave in a notebook must be one you actually
fetched successfully in this run. Never invent record numbers, file paths or table names.

Tasks:
1. ch04/ex04_2.ipynb and ch04/ex04_2_solution.ipynb (exercise: "recreate a plot from a recent CMS or ATLAS paper"). The current
   HEPData record https://www.hepdata.net/record/ins2931458 is WRONG: it is a CMS D0→μμ search, but the code expects a
   Higgs pT table "PT(H)". Find, via the HEPData search/API (e.g. https://www.hepdata.net/search/?q=...&format=json and
   https://www.hepdata.net/record/insNNNN?format=json), a real CMS (preferably) or ATLAS record with a differential Higgs
   cross section vs pT(H), or another clean, well-known published distribution if a Higgs one is impractical. Use the exact
   table name and the correct JSON access pattern (check how HEPData returns a single table: e.g. `?format=json&table=...`
   or the `/record/data/<recid>/<table_id>/<version>` style that the record JSON points to). Fetch it, parse it, and draw
   the plot in the solution. Update the markdown (paper title, arXiv or DOI as given by HEPData, experiment, √s), the axis
   labels and units exactly as in the table headers. Keep a clear fallback message if the network is unavailable.
2. ch01/ex01_4*.ipynb and ch11/ex11_1*.ipynb currently use toy data because no verified open-data URL was known. Find
   real, public, small files on the CERN Open Data portal (https://opendata.cern.ch, API: https://opendata.cern.ch/api/records/?q=...&type=Dataset
   and https://opendata.cern.ch/api/records/<recid>) or ATLAS Open Data (https://opendata.atlas.cern):
   - ex01_4 ("inspect a sample dataset's structure with ROOT or uproot, identify branches, estimate event size"): pick
     a small file (ideally < 200 MB, ≤ 1 GB at most) readable with uproot over HTTPS (root:// XRootD URLs also work with uproot
     via fsspec-xrootd, but prefer HTTPS). Open it with uproot here to confirm the tree name and some branch names, and
     use those exact names.
   - ex11_1 ("download a public CMS NanoAOD file and implement a Z→μμ selection, measure the Z mass; Golden JSON"):
     a real CMS 2016 NanoAOD (Run 2 open data) file URL of a DoubleMuon or SingleMuon dataset, plus the matching certified-
     luminosity (Golden) JSON URL from the portal. Verify both by fetching (for the ROOT file, open it with uproot and
     read the Muon_pt, Muon_eta, Muon_phi, Muon_charge, run and luminosityBlock branches for a few events; read only a
     limited entry range such as entry_stop=200000 to keep Colab runtime low). Implement the certification filter with
     the JSON in the solution.
   Keep the toy-data path only as an automatic fallback when the download fails, and label it as such.
3. Scan ALL notebooks (ch*/**.ipynb) for any other http(s)/root:// data URLs. Check each one (HTTP status 200 or a
   successful uproot open). Fix or remove broken ones. Do not change the Colab badge links or the colab.research.google.com URLs.

Local environment: install what you need into a temporary venv or with `pip install --user` (uproot, awkward, fsspec-xrootd
optional, requests). Do not commit any downloaded data files.

Constraints: keep notebook structure and conventions (seeded RNG, IN_COLAB guards, `# TODO` in student notebooks, no
answers in student notebooks, outputs cleared, valid nbformat v4). Do not touch anything outside ch*/ except updating
ch*/README.md tables if titles change. Do not run git commit or push.

Verify (run and report output):
  - For every URL you placed: the command you used to fetch it and the result (status, size, tree/branch names or table name).
  - Execute ex04_2_solution.ipynb and ex11_1_solution.ipynb (and ex01_4_solution.ipynb) locally in-process or with nbconvert,
    and report the key printed result (for 11.1, the fitted/measured Z mass with its uncertainty, and the number of selected events).
  - Then clear all outputs again and validate with nbformat.
Report: the final URLs, what each file is (dataset name, record id), results, and anything not resolved.
